name: Chandrayaan-1
tagline: India went to the Moon with a set of questions—and returned evidence that changed how we look at its dusty surface.
credit: Original editorial illustration created for the Left Behind archive.

beats.goal: Map the Moon’s chemical, mineralogical and photo-geologic features using an international suite of scientific instruments.
beats.achieved: The spacecraft completed more than 3,400 lunar orbits and contributed to the discovery of widespread water/hydroxyl signatures on the lunar surface. Its Moon Impact Probe also reached the surface.
beats.ending: Communication with the orbiter was lost on August 29, 2009, after the mission had completed its major objectives.
beats.now: The Chandrayaan-1 orbiter is no longer operational. Its orbit later decayed, and it remains a landmark mission in India’s planetary exploration history.
beats.learned: The mission established India as a lunar exploration nation and demonstrated the value of international payload collaboration.
